combEvidence: The main Wadi 'Ara/Triangle villages 'did not budge and were allowed to stay' (25-30,000) under the 3 April armistice cession from Jordan. Peaceful territorial transfer, no Israeli assault; passage is silent on any wartime combatant presence in these villages.

event: After repeated returns to this Western-Galilee village (conquered May 1948 in Operation Ben-'Ami), the Military Government ordered all villagers to leave within 48 hours; they complied, moving to Sheikh Daoud and eventually al Mazra'a. The expulsion raised a hue and cry in Mapam.
quote: On 24 January 1950, the Military Government ordered all the villagers to leave within 48 hours, and they complied.
scaleNote: No alternative accommodation prepared; returning resettlers later jailed; Kibbutz Evron cultivated 1,500 dunams of Ghabisiya land
causeNote: Mapam-dominated settlements bloc publicly endorsed the eviction despite Mapam's leadership condemning it; the village was slated for settlement

event: After the appalling health/food situation and a January 1950 Ben-Gurion decision to evict 'without coercion', General Staff approved the transfer of Zakariya's Arabs to Lydda and Ramle (19 March). On 9 June they were evicted: some chose resettlement in Ramle/Lydda, the majority opted for the West Bank, ending up in the Deheishe refugee camp near Bethlehem.
quote: On 9 June, they were evicted, some preferring resettlement in Ramle and Lydda; others, perhaps the majority, opted for the West Bank
scaleNote: Interior Ministry had eyed Zakariya's 'many good houses' for new immigrants; ~160 inhabitants, only ~20 able to work
causeNote: Eviction 'without coercion'; land-owners wishing to leave bought out

No combatants/arms/resistance; an administrative transfer of a destitute remnant.

event: On 2 September 1950, according to the United Nations, some 4,000 beduin were reportedly driven into Egyptian-held Sinai. Israel said the true figure was in 'the hundreds' and that they were 'infiltrees'.

event: After Allon's (1949) and Dayan's (Nov 1949) campaigns and a 14 Jan 1950 decision to transfer 'without coercion', the ~2,600 Arabs of the barbed-wired Majdal 'ghetto' were trucked to the Gaza Strip. >100 went Feb-March; the formal transfer began 14 June (38 to the Gaza border); the last transports left for Gaza and Lydda on 12-13 October. Majdal was the last big post-1948 transfer operation.
quote: Majdal was the last big post-1948 transfer operation.
scaleNote: Final transports of those wishing to stay required coercion 'of the sort used in Faluja' — nighttime shots, arrests of leaders, banging on doors with rifle butts; ~200 Qatra refugees sent to Ramle
causeNote: Carrots-and-sticks: oppressive movement/employment restrictions plus favourable currency exchange to induce 'voluntary' departure to relatives in Gaza

srcNote: Carrots-and-sticks: oppressive movement/employment restrictions plus favourable currency exchange to induce 'voluntary' departure to relatives in Gaza
combEvidence: This is the June-Oct 1950 administrative transfer of ~2,600 residual Arabs (mostly returnee civilians under military government in a barbed-wire 'ghetto') to Gaza — no combatants. At the Nov 1948 conquest the Egyptian brigade HQ and garrison had already withdrawn and the IDF was 'greeted by 11 elders who asked to surrender the town' (Birth p.473), so resisted=no. Allon's transfer proposal claimed Majdal 'served as a base for enemy infiltration and for small hostile actions' (p.528) — but that is an attacker-side justification about 1949-50 infiltration, not a documented village attack, so launched=unknown.

event: Khirbet al Jalama, one of the largest khurab (~225 inhabitants), was emptied on 1 March 1950. The inhabitants petitioned the High Court, which in June 1952 ruled in their favour; but before they could return, members of Kibbutz Lehavot Haviva (Mapam), settled on the khirbe's lands, blew up the remaining Arab houses on 11 August 1953, assuring no return.

perp: Military Government; later Kibbutz Lehavot Haviva
scaleNote: High Court authorized return (June 1952) but the kibbutz demolition (with claimed army funds) preempted it
causeNote: Court-ordered return defeated by destruction of the site — a broken-return outcome paralleling Iqrit/Bir'im
